ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.05 as a Ryde voucher for the non-exempt off-route kilometre; no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is RydeTAXI, metered, so extra distance is billed and any non-exempt off-route kilometre is refundable under RD-2 [F7]. The trace settles that exactly one off-route segment exists [F3] (RD-1), and that no qualifying traffic incident stood on the replaced stretch [F14] (RD-4(a) fails; the Pan Island Expressway band-2 record [F12] is corroborating speed-band evidence only and cannot exempt by itself under RD-4(b)). So the case turns on the RD-5 consent question.

Timing and authorship: the driver offered an alternative at 12:24 [F8] and the rider herself replied at 12:25, before the segment began at 12:27 [F9]. Her words "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" read as "up to you, take whichever way is faster, I'm in a hurry" — a general route authorisation, not a refusal and not a named road [F9]. The driver's post-trip statement [F11] merely restates that agreement and adds nothing; a driver's own claim of consent is not consent (G11), but here the rider's own message supplies it [F9][RD-5].

Scope of that authorisation: "whichever way is faster" is a route choice made to reach the destination, and the measured segment is exactly such a route choice, driven after the rider's own pre-segment message [F3][F9][RD-5]. It is not an errand of the driver's own, not a stop away from the route, and not a loop reaching nothing — the record shows no stop at all in the segment [F3][F8][F9]. The authorisation therefore covers the segment's extra kilometres, so the whole deviation is not refundable; what remains recoverable is the excess-distance charge actually billed for that deviation [F3][F4][RD-2]. RD-3 gives no independent exemption: the rider named no place and no stop was measured, so her message was a route authorisation, not a stop request [F3][F8][F9][RD-3(a)].

Amount from the fare record: this trip's rate is its distance fare ÷ distance km = $25.39 ÷ 18.01 km = $1.4098/km as the record states it [F4][F7]. The billed excess distance is $4.06 for 2.88 km [F4]; at the same rate the segment's own extra kilometres are 2.16 km [F3], so the refundable portion is 2.16 km × $1.4098/km = $3.0452, i.e. $3.05 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The remaining ~$1.01 of the excess-distance charge is mileage not attributed to the segment and is not refundable under RD-2 [F1][F3][F4]. The waiting charge $0.11 [F5] is a RydeTAXI meter waiting unit and is not refunded under RD-3(c); no surge applied [F6].

Account action: the driver has 0 prior upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], so RD-6 is not triggered and no account flag is added [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages [F8][F9] and the driver's statement [F11]; they contain only a route offer, the rider's assent and a fare grievance — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is none [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1].

Evidence: the chat is complete with every message timestamped [F10], the segment is measured [F3], and all fare components are recorded [F4][F7], so the record settles every element this ruling needs [F3][F4][F7][F10].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's pre-segment message '随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间' [F9], sent after the driver's offer [F8], is a general route authorisation to reach the destination rather than consent to any particular route being taken as far as the fare is concerned; RD-5 confines its effect to the route choice, so the measured segment's 2.16 extra km remain within the refundable excess-distance charge under RD-2 [F3][F4]. Its extra kilometres are the ones billed at $1.4098/km and are refunded as the partial amount.
